stanzas: Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Suivant la maxime de l’Évangile,
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Du législateur tout s’accomplira.
Celui qui s’élève, on l’abaissera ;
Celui qui s’abaisse, l’on élèvera.
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Le vrai catéchisme nous instruira,
Et l’affreux fanatisme s’éteindra.
Pour être à la loi docile,
Tout Français s’exercera.
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Pierrette et Margot chantent à la guinguette ;
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Réjouissons-nous, le bon temps viendra !
Le peuple français, jadis à quia ;
L’aristocrate dit mea culpa !
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Le clergé regrette le bien qu’il a ;
Par justice la nation l’aura.
Par le prudent Lafayette,
Tout trouble s’apaisera.
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Par les flambeaux de l’auguste assemblée,
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Le peuple armé toujours se gardera.
Le vrai d’avec le faux l’on connaîtra ;
Le citoyen pour le bien soutiendra.
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
quand l’aristocrate protestera,
Le bon citoyen au nez lui rira,
Sans avoir l’âme troublée,
Toujours le plus fort sera.
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Petits comme grands sont soldats dans l’âme,
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Pendant la guerre aucun ne trahira.
Avec cœur tout bon Français combattra ;
S’il voit du louche, hardiment parlera.
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Lafayette dit : "Vienne qui voudra !
Le patriotisme leur répondra ! "
Sans craindre ni feu ni flamme,
Le Français toujours vaincra !
Ah ! ça ira, ça ira, ça ira !
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Following the maxim of the Gospel,
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
All of the lawgiver's word will be fulfilled.
He who raises himself, he shall be brought low;
He who lowers himself, he shall be raised up.
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
The true catechism will instruct us,
And dreadful fanaticism will die out.
To be obedient to the law,
Every Frenchman will train himself.
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Pierrette and Margot sing at the tavern;
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Let us rejoice, the good times will come!
The French people, once left without an answer;
The aristocrat says mea culpa!
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
The clergy mourns the wealth it has;
By justice the nation will have it.
Through the prudent Lafayette,
All unrest will calm down.
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
By the torches of the august assembly,
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
The armed people will always keep guard over itself.
The true from the false will be known;
The citizen will stand up for the good.
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
when the aristocrat protests,
The good citizen will laugh in his face,
Without having his soul troubled,
[He] will always be the stronger.
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Small and great alike are soldiers at heart,
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
During the war none will betray.
With courage every good Frenchman will fight;
If he sees something shady, he will speak out boldly.
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!
Lafayette says: "Come who will!
Patriotism will answer them!"
Without fearing either fire or flame,
The Frenchman will always win!
Ah! it will go, it will go, it will go!

notes: General (the refrain): 'ça ira', literally 'it will go', means 'it will work out, it will succeed'; translated literally each time it stands. This is Ladré's 1790 text, from the time of the Fête de la Fédération; the later, violent refrain ('les aristocrates à la lanterne') is not in it.

line 1.4: 'Du législateur tout s'accomplira', 'everything of the lawgiver will be fulfilled'. The lawgiver is most likely Christ, the giver of the Gospel's law (the next two lines paraphrase Luke 14:11); a reading as the National Assembly, the legislator of the day, is possible.
lines 1.5-1.6: 'l'on élèvera', literally 'one will raise'; rendered in the passive.
line 1.8: 'the true catechism' is set against 'fanaticism' (in the period's sense: religious bigotry).
line 2.2: Pierrette and Margot are stock names for working women; a 'guinguette' is a suburban open-air tavern with dancing.
line 2.5: 'à quia', a Latin tag: reduced to silence, unable to answer; the line has no verb in the original.
line 2.6: 'mea culpa' is Latin, 'through my fault', from the confession; kept as in the original.
lines 2.8-2.9: the Church's property was put at the nation's disposal in November 1789; 'regrette' here: is sorry for (losing) the wealth it has.
line 3.2: 'flambeaux', torches: the lights (enlightenment) of the National Assembly.
line 3.5: 'l'on connaîtra', literally 'one will know'; rendered in the passive.
line 3.8: lower-case 'quand' as in the source.
line 3.11: the original has no subject on this line ('Toujours le plus fort sera'); 'He' (the good citizen) is supplied.
line 4.5: 'Avec cœur', with heart, i.e. with courage.
line 4.6: 'du louche', something shady or suspicious.
